title: Learning about children's rights
summary: Review rights that protect all children and responsibilities that help us live together.
keyIdeas: All children around the world have the same rights, without discrimination.
We have rights to health, education, play and family care.
Alongside our rights, we have a responsibility to respect others.

basicKnowledge: C. Sociedades y territorios › Alfabetización cívica

activities.prompt: All children have the right to go to school.
activities.explanation: Education is a basic right that helps all children learn and grow.

activities.prompt: Omar has a high fever at home. Which right protects his access to care?
activities.explanation: The right to health includes getting medical care when Omar is ill.
activities.hint: Think about a hospital or health centre.
options: The right to travel by plane

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence about a child's identity.
activities.explanation: Having a name identifies us and is part of our right to an identity.
activities.sentence: Every child has the right to a ___ and a nationality from birth.

activities.prompt: Match each right to an everyday example.
activities.explanation: Rights help protect us as we grow.

activities.prompt: Children only have rights when they get very good marks.
activities.explanation: Rights belong to every child. Children do not have to earn them by getting good marks.

activities.prompt: Sort these examples into rights or responsibilities.
activities.explanation: Rights protect us. Responsibilities help us live well together.

activities.prompt: Aisha wants to share an idea for the school festival. She has the right to:
activities.explanation: All children have the right to express their views and be listened to.
activities.hint: Good classmates listen to each other.
options: Give orders to all the other children

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence about care at home.
activities.explanation: All children deserve love, protection and care, whatever their family situation.
activities.sentence: All children have the right to protection and ___ at home.

activities.prompt: Match each public service to the right it protects.
activities.explanation: Hospitals care for our health, and schools support our education.

activities.prompt: A child works so many hours that they cannot attend school or rest. Why does this violate their rights?
activities.explanation: Work that prevents learning or rest, or harms health, violates children's rights.
activities.hint: Remember the rights to learn, rest and be protected.
options: They need education, rest and protection from exploitation
They should only work without being paid
Studying only matters when they are an adult
